description: Detection rate per fault family. Faults are injected into a clean synthetic stream and a clean synthetic code corpus; a fault counts as detected when the tool reports the expected finding at the injected place.

families.description: event name misspelled (last character dropped)
a required property removed
a property that is not in the plan added
an integer property sent as a string
an integer property sent with a fraction
a boolean property sent as the string "true" or "false"
an enum property set to a value that is not listed
an enum value with its first letter capitalised
an enum property swapped for a different listed value
families.note: Both values are allowed by the plan, so a plan cannot call either wrong.

families.description: an event delivered twice with the same event_id
an event retried with a new event_id and everything else the same
families.note: Only the event_id is compared; the same content under a new id is a different event as far as the tool can tell.

families.description: a user's first workspace_created moved before their signup_completed
a user's signup_completed event removed, leaving later steps
families.note: A stream can start in the middle of a funnel, so a missing earlier step is not reported; only steps seen out of order are.

families.description: received_at later than the 15 minute tolerance (16 minutes to 6 hours)
a timestamp later than receive time by more than the 5 minute tolerance (6 minutes to 2 hours)
an email address in an undeclared string property
a phone number written (555) 010-0xxx
a phone number written 555-010-0xxx
a phone number written +44 20 7946 0xxx
a phone number as ten bare digits
families.note: Ten bare digits look like any numeric id, so the detector does not match them.

families.description: an email address written "name dot x at example dot com"
families.note: Only the usual local-part@domain shape is matched.

families.description: a person's name
families.note: A name has no fixed shape; the detector matches shapes, not meaning.

families.description: a street address
families.note: Same reason as names: no fixed shape.

families.description: a line cut off in the middle (invalid JSON)
user_id missing from the envelope
ts written "2026-11-02 10:00:00" (no T, no offset)

highCardinality.description: 80 signup events in a 600-user stream given unique referrer values (plan bound 40); 50 streams per seed, each also run without the injection as a control

code.generator: scripts/code-corpus.ts, calls built from the example plan in several syntaxes (track, analytics.track, analytics?.track; three quote styles; single-line and multi-line; quoted keys; .ts, .tsx and .js files)

families.description: an email address literal in an undeclared string property

a phone number literal as ten bare digits

families.description: the event name passed in a variable
families.note: Reported as non-literal-event-name: the tool says it cannot check the call, and the run fails.

families.description: a misspelled event name held in a const declared above the call
families.note: The tool reads only literals in the call, so it reports the call as unverifiable instead of naming the typo.

families.description: a required property missing from an object passed by variable
families.note: The properties are not an object literal, so the tool says it cannot read them.

families.description: a required property missing, with a spread in the object literal
families.note: A spread may or may not supply the property, so the tool reports it as unverifiable.

families.description: a misspelled event name passed to a wrapper (logEvent) that is not a configured tracker
families.note: Only the configured tracker names are matched, so a wrapper is never seen unless it is passed with --tracker.

families.description: a misspelled event name passed through const t = analytics.track
families.note: An alias has a different name from any configured tracker.

families.description: a misspelled event name passed to analytics['track']
families.note: Calls through bracket access are not matched.

families.description: an integer property given String(count)
families.note: A value that is not a literal is not compared; the run reports how many such values it skipped.
